summary: Same rules, packages, listing and (message, instant) give the same classification, action and codes
No network request to decide on a message in Active or Transition
Integration is network configuration only; forwarded bodies are byte-identical
In-force dates come only from the hub records and listing
Bytes of immutable routes never change
Versions of registered agreements stay obtainable
expand, migrate, contract; rejects only after enforced_from + L with minimum grace
Without freshness beyond max_staleness, enforce rejects every message
Records, listings and manifests carry a proof verifiable with an assertionMethod key
No namespace operation reads or modifies another namespace
Drafts failing N1–N5 or LIFECYCLE_* are rejected with one problem per finding
Candidates are immutable; approve and reject only from open
No release without approval of a steward of the namespace
Release steps run in order; failures leave nothing visible
Dates follow the §3.3.2 table with the minimum grace
Approval fails on DATE-1 or DATE-2
Emitted dates never change; revoked_from is added once
Listings on date changes and at most every ttl/2, sequence +1, validity ttl
versions[] follows the membership rule
eddsa-jcs-2022 proofs with an assertionMethod verification method
Immutable routes serve the same bytes with ETag = SHA-256
Version listing and records are Cache-Control no-cache
Releases, artefacts, revisions, blobs and events are never modified
Revocation follows REV-1..REV-4 and issues a listing
Never sign with a key absent from assertionMethod; check own DID
GET /pub/{ns} answers 303 to the head
Non-public operations require a valid token and the §3.5 table
PUT drafts requires If-Match (428) and checks it (412)
Missing /v1 resources are API_NOT_FOUND
Every effectful operation emits an event with increasing id
A record equals its entry in the last listing
Token validation follows A1–A5 in order
Steward membership is evaluated on every request
Namespaces are isolated and have their own sequence
Slug pattern, unique, immutable, _vhub reserved
Vocabulary fields, content, size, revisions and dereferencing URLs
Upstream fetched only on create and refresh, never by /pub
Same bytes create no new revision
/v1 responses are compact JSON-LD, errors included
/pub/_vhub/v1 serves the A.5 context byte for byte and vocab.ttl
Credentials have the common form of §3.8
Startup checks CFG-1 and CFG-2 and exits non-zero with the code
Onboarding classification until the first E1
Sync at start and within the head sync_interval
S1–S7 on every listing
Sequence, dates and DID cache survive restarts
A failing version in S7–S13 discards the whole listing
A package is used whole or not at all
State machine of §4.5
V_t with lease margin
JSON-LD expansion resolves only manifest URLs
Classification follows the §4.7 pseudocode
Actions follow the mode and combination tables
Responses to the sender follow §4.8
Bodies and headers unchanged; only VHub-Verdict added
Agreement capture rules, before answering
Admission table and AGREEMENT_REVOCATION_SCHEDULED
Packages of agreement versions are kept
Degraded and FailClosed classification
Admin API never on DSP or management listeners
GET /status fields
Events of §4.12; vhub.verdict validates against A.4
No rule gives default_action
Passive audit of §4.11
Proof verification V0–V4
CLOCK_SKEW_EXCEEDED beyond clock_skew
Unknown agreement or rule id is API_NOT_FOUND
did:web resolution at did_ttl and at most once a minute on bad proofs
Rule changes need If-Match and RULE-1..5 on the whole set
One rule revision per message; vhub.rules on change
Rule selection follows select_rule
Rule set survives restarts; seed only with an empty store
:explain decides like the hot path without effects
Package collection of §4.10
SYNC_MALFORMED on shape, @context, issuer or namespace
Listing validates against A.1
Version record validates against A.2
Client configuration validates against A.3
vhub.verdict validates against A.4
